03 / Tints and shades

Every step, with a number.

Six complete brand scales, including warm white and mist. The 500 step preserves the supplied base. Lighter and darker derivatives below are proposed working tokens.

Derived proposal

Tints: blend toward brand white

Accent endpoint: warm white #F5F7FA. Steps 50 / 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 blend 95% / 90% / 75% / 50% / 25% toward this endpoint. Warm-white and mist neutral tints use #FFFFFF so their steps remain distinct.

Shades: blend toward brand navy

Accent endpoint: navy #101925. Steps 600 / 700 / 800 / 900 / 950 blend 15% / 30% / 45% / 60% / 75% toward this endpoint. The navy neutral scale instead shades toward #000000. The 500 base stays exact.

Encoded sRGB formula: round(base × (1 − mix) + endpoint × mix), channel by channel. Accent and semantic scales use brand warm white and navy. Neutral exceptions are labeled per row: navy shades toward black; warm-white and mist tints toward pure white. Each family has eleven distinct steps. Semantic aliases intentionally reuse their brand family. These proposed mixtures are not perceptually uniform. Select any chip to copy its hex.

Check any pairing

Normal text requires at least 4.5:1; large text and meaningful non-text boundaries require 3:1. Large text is at least 24 CSS px regular or about 18.67px bold. State labels and icons remain required. W3C contrast guidance.

Aa · A clear message in every state.

Search by color, token, semantic alias, or hex. The list includes opaque palette, supporting, and derived colors; transparent dividers depend on their underlying surface.

Usage rules. Use success for a confirmed result; pending uses neutral styling plus “Connecting…” or “Translating…”. Warning indicates a condition needing attention; danger explains failure and recovery. Information provides context; translation labels do not certify accuracy. Preserve user input on failure. Never rely on hue alone.

A 4:3 modular type scale

Base: 16px (1rem). Ratio: 4 ÷ 3 = 1.333333…
Step n = 16 × (4/3)ⁿ. Each step is one third larger than the previous step. Table sizes are rounded; CSS tokens retain nine decimal places in rem.

:root {
  --type-minus-1: 0.750000000rem; /* 12.000000px at 16px root */
  --type-0: 1.000000000rem; /* 16.000000px at 16px root */
  --type-1: 1.333333333rem; /* 21.333333px at 16px root */
  --type-2: 1.777777778rem; /* 28.444444px at 16px root */
  --type-3: 2.370370370rem; /* 37.925926px at 16px root */
  --type-4: 3.160493827rem; /* 50.567901px at 16px root */
  --type-5: 4.213991770rem; /* 67.423868px at 16px root */
  --leading-body: 1.6;
  --leading-complex-script: 1.7;
}
/* Responsive display uses discrete modular steps. */
.hero-title { font-size: var(--type-5); line-height: 1.1; }
@media (max-width:1080px) { .hero-title { font-size:var(--type-4); } }
@media (max-width:720px) { .hero-title { font-size:var(--type-3); } }
.message { font-size:var(--type-0); line-height:1.6; }
.message:lang(th), .message:lang(km) { line-height:1.7; }

Responsive rule: desktop hero step 5 = 67.424px, tablet step 4 = 50.568px, mobile step 3 = 37.926px. Body stays at step 0 (16px); never shrink messages to fit. Rem tokens follow the user’s root font size. Short metadata may use step −1 (12px); fixed 14px labels are legacy guide details outside the proposed modular scale.

Multilingual rule: compact 1.1–1.3 display leading is for short Latin headlines. UI/message copy starts at 1.6; Thai, Khmer, and Indic text starts at 1.7 and needs stacked-mark verification. Locale-aware JP / SC / TC / HK / KR fonts, native shaping, and content-driven height take priority over compact line boxes. Allow wrapping, 200% enlargement, and user text-spacing overrides.

Geometry note: sizes describe CSS pixels at a 16px root. Device pixels and screenshot pixels vary with zoom and display scale. The Aa specimens use the actual token font sizes, not scaled images.

How language-aware typography works

The UI locale sets the page language. Original messages keep their source language; translated messages get their target language. Unknown or mixed content must not inherit a falsely certain language.

Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Taiwan Traditional Chinese, Hong Kong Traditional Chinese and Korean can share characters but need different glyph conventions. Correct language tags select the appropriate JP/SC/TC/HK/KR face.

Self-hosted WOFF2 subsets should load only when displayed content needs them. That includes language-picker labels, not just the current UI. Keep system emoji and missing-glyph fallback. This is scoped script support, not complete Unicode coverage.

Squircle buttons, across the system

Buttons echo the smooth continuous corners of the Comett mark. The fuller 24px corner token adds a little more curvature; the chat window uses a related 32px token, with a 24px rounded fallback. The button shape is inspired by the logo; it does not redraw or alter the approved artwork.

TokenSupported browserFallback
--comett-button-radius1.5rem / 24px at 16px root1.125rem / 18px at 16px root
--comett-button-corner-shapesquircleround
--comett-room-radius2rem / 32px1.5rem / 24px, round
Hit areaAt least 48px high; icon-only target remains 48 × 48px.
Focus3px outline with 4px offset. No mask or clip-path on controls; ancestors leave focus visible.
:root {
  --comett-button-radius: 1.125rem;
  --comett-button-corner-shape: round;
}
@supports (corner-shape: squircle) {
  :root {
    --comett-button-radius: 1.5rem;
    --comett-button-corner-shape: squircle;
  }
}
button {
  border-radius: var(--comett-button-radius);
  corner-shape: var(--comett-button-corner-shape);
  min-height: 3rem;
}

Responsive behavior: use the same shape tokens at mobile and desktop sizes. Keep padding and the hit area; let long labels wrap and controls grow vertically. The theme switch’s outer button follows this rule while its celestial thumb remains circular. Inputs retain their separate 12px field corners.

States keep their meaning: coral fill for primary actions, an outlined secondary action, explicit disabled state, and visible focus. Squircle corners apply to color-copy buttons, dropdown triggers, the theme control, icon buttons, and button-style links. Swatch buttons have gaps so each shape and focus ring is visible.

Corner-shape support varies. The rounded fallback is always usable. Native borders and outlines follow supported corner shapes. CSS Borders specification.

Hover, press, and focus

Actions respond consistently. A fine pointer gets a 2.5% scale-up, a 2px lift, and a soft brand-colored glow over 160ms. Transforms preserve layout spacing. Primary actions tint to coral-400; their navy label stays readable. Outlined controls gain a clearer border and raised surface.

InteractionRule
Hover · mouse / trackpad2.5% scale-up, 2px lift, subtle glow and shadow, 160ms easing. Primary glow stays coral; secondary controls use teal. Dropdowns keep their center anchored with a smaller 1% scale.
PressReturn to resting scale with a 1px press and shorter 80ms feedback. Primary fill returns to coral-500. Open dropdowns and enabled toggles retain a visible inset edge.
Color-copy controlsKeep the exact displayed hex fill. A current-color inset edge, glow, and shadow show interaction; the fill stays exact.
Keyboard focusPreserve the 3px outline and 4px offset; swatches retain their inset focus treatment. Hero links use warm white against the navy panel.
Touch / coarse pointerHover feedback is limited to devices with a fine pointer and hover support. Tap keeps press feedback without a sticky hover state.
Reduced motion / disabledReduced motion removes movement and transitions while retaining color and border feedback. Disabled actions keep their resting appearance.

Interaction tokens: --comett-hover-scale: 1.025; --comett-hover-lift: -2px; --comett-interaction-duration: 160ms. Use the button examples above to inspect the states in both themes.

One custom picker, consistent behavior

The state and sample-language selectors use a shared component, modeled on Comett’s public pre-join language picker. Search, selected indication, Enter selection, outside click, and Escape dismissal match the app pattern. Arrow keys and Home / End move through results; Tab keeps a natural focus order. Selection returns focus to the trigger.

Caret spacing: a dedicated 20px column, 16px gap, and 16px inline padding. Labels wrap without colliding with the 16px caret. Controls stay at least 48px tall.

Full theme: use the animated day/night switch to change all page surfaces, text, fields, popup menus, messages, borders, and focus rings. Explicit palette and light/dark comparison specimens preserve their displayed color values.

Inspected live at Comett’s pre-join page on 5 November 2026. No room was created or joined. Native selects remain a fallback when JavaScript is unavailable. The screenshot’s “Inspect a state” control identifies this guide as the requested target; application code is unchanged.

08 / Chatroom atmosphere

A little atmosphere.
Space to talk.

A sparse star field gives the room depth. Distant points are smaller, dimmer, and softer; nearer coral, teal, lilac, and neutral pinpoints move a little more as the conversation scrolls.

Interactive proposal
Room A7K4QFictional conversation · local demo
Preview only

Nothing is sent to a room or translation service.

Local preview. Scroll within the conversation or add a sample message.

Far · atmosphere

48 tiny, softened points per tile. Low opacity reduces contrast and saturation. Travel follows 0.9% of scrolling plus a 1.35px forward arrival impulse.

Middle · distance

30 slightly clearer points per tile. Travel follows 2.2% of scrolling plus a 3.3px forward arrival impulse.

Near · pinpoints

18 sharper brand-color points. The nearest layer moves the most, with a forward 7.5px impulse when a message arrives, plus 5% of the conversation’s scroll distance. Pattern wrapping is visually seamless.

Motion and readability rules. Keep the field decorative and behind opaque message surfaces. Use passive scroll handling, one short, settling animation per event batch, and three layer transforms; there is no idle animation loop. A fixed 600px SVG pattern repeats seamlessly inside the visible chat window, with 48px of overscan and one spare tile; it does not grow with the message list or use Houdini. Continuous travel follows scroll deltas plus a forward arrival impulse; trimming old messages and responsive line wrapping rebase the scroll coordinate without reversing the field. The canvas is pure white in light theme and navy-600 in dark theme. Incoming messages use the very light warm-white-500 neutral in light theme. Light stars use the vibrant coral-500, teal-500, and lilac-500 colors, plus navy-500, at 35 / 65 / 100% far-to-near opacity; dark stars use the base brand colors and warm-white-500 at 28 / 46 / 78%. The nearest light-theme points render at their full brand color; size and softness preserve atmospheric perspective. Both incoming and own messages use the same deliberate two-part shadow, adjusted for the theme. The preview retains at most 40 messages. Pause depth motion, or enable the system’s reduced-motion preference, for a static field and immediate scrolling. Light and dark themes adjust the atmosphere without changing message meaning. This is a guide proposal; production behavior is unchanged.
09 / Brand in motion

Familiar orbit.
New identity.

The orbital animation from the Comett portfolio case study, rebuilt with the approved squircle and design-system palette.

Interactive proposal
Motion exploration · soft gravity, free passage. Three brand-colored points keep moving around the C while softly attracting one another. They can pass through each other; contact never triggers a bounce or separation constraint. A gentle orbital guide and smooth radial restoring forces prevent lingering pairs and keep the flow contained. Short traces reveal changing paths, and close passes send faint connection rings. The C shifts and tilts slightly in response to the combined gravitational field, using a damped spring capped by a soft target of about 2.4px per axis and 1.4 degrees at a 340px orbit. Its approved outline remains unchanged. This is an art-directed model with a fixed 120Hz step. The pause switch in Accessibility freezes the scene; hidden or off-screen previews stop processing and resume from the same positions. System reduced motion keeps the whole arrangement static. These decorative signals do not indicate actual messages or status. Original portfolio case study.

11 / Built for reading

Clarity is part of the identity.

A good system survives a small screen, a long translation, a different script, and someone’s personal reading settings.

Acceptance criteria
  • AA text contrast and visible focus
  • Logical keyboard and reading order
  • Language tags and safe bidi handling
  • No clipped marks or fixed-height text boxes
  • Test at 320px, 375px and desktop
  • Check zoom and larger text settings
  • Respect reduced motion
  • Verify font failures and mixed-script messages
Decorative motion. The brand orbit pauses off screen and follows your system’s reduced-motion preference. You can also pause it here.
